recent_posts.topic_title: Introducing Streak: your matchday predictions, settled on CKB
recent_posts.author: 0xTonraq
recent_posts.content_text:
Home win, a stubborn draw, or the upset everyone else dismissed?
I’m building Streak to give your predictions a complete on-chain journey: choose an outcome, fund your position, follow the match and collect your return.
Streak is a sports prediction platform on CKB testnet, starting with football. Alongside prediction markets, there are free weekly fantasy and Survivor games. Payments and rewards currently use testnet tCKB, not real-money prizes.
01-markets1920×1380 232 KB
Desktop and mobile views of the actual app, using synthetic local fixtures for this gallery.
One slip for your matchday
Browse by day or league, open a fixture and choose Home, Draw or Away. Pool information shows how participating stakes are distributed; your potential return depends on the final pool and published rules.
Put up to eight predictions into one slip and approve one wallet payment. Each settles independently: one wrong call does not cancel another winning position.
Before signing, review your stakes, network fee and refundable CKB storage. A 100 tCKB prediction currently requires another 321 tCKB in refundable position storage, plus its fee. The wallet total should never be a surprise.
Activity keeps accepted positions, pending transactions and collectable returns together, without requiring you to become a blockchain explorer expert.
Keep browsing while your payment confirms
Recent wallet work covers restoring authorized connections, switching accounts, retaining drafts and recovering interrupted submissions.
On mobile, minimize a pending payment into an animated three-cell tracker. Move it to a corner and tap for details. Monitoring continues while you browse, avoiding the slip, navigation and dialogs.
02-payment-tracking1920×1381 252 KB
A synthetic pending payment demonstrates the tracker. This is an interface capture, not a live transaction receipt.
What happens after the final whistle?
The configured football oracle reports results. CKB contracts enforce the resulting settlement and payout rules, creating separate claims that users can collect independently.
Winning positions receive their calculated return and recoverable storage. Losing positions still recover their storage deposit. Collection also has a network fee, shown before signing. Void, timeout and late-entry cases follow their respective refund rules.
Streak saves signed transaction bytes before submission and follows that original payment during recovery. A lost response should not become another request to pay.
03-activity1920×1381 215 KB
The same Activity screen at both sizes, populated with synthetic local history.
Building around CKB, and learning from slow screens
First, provisioning every fixture in advance tied up capacity in markets nobody might use. Now the first prediction creates an eligible market, with Streak supplying its reserve capacity. New and existing markets can share one payment.
Second, Activity originally searched market by market for a wallet’s positions. A central tracking cell looked tempting, but making every update consume and replace the same cell would create contention.
The solution combines shared Rust scripts and separate market, deposit and claim cells with an event-driven wallet index. Payment and settlement observations update the affected records, so opening Activity becomes a database read. Replay and targeted reconciliation handle missed updates and chain reorganisations.
The index makes discovery faster; it cannot grant a payout. Collection still validates actual on-chain spending conditions. The football oracle remains a trust assumption too: the blockchain enforces the rules, but does not independently know the score.
Prediction architecture · Activity design and measurements
A reason to come back every gameweek
Predictions are the foundation. Two beta games offer additional ways to join in without placing a stake:
Streak Five: pick five EPL players within 40 credits and choose a double-points captain. Real performances earn points, and each gameweek starts fresh. It uses FPL player data and official deadlines, with Streak’s own scoring rules. How Fantasy Premier League works.
Survivor: choose one winning team each round, but never reuse a team. Save a favourite for later or use it to stay alive now. Full Survivor rules.
04-streak-five1920×1381 263 KB
The actual Five interface at both sizes, using isolated sample gameweek data.
05-streak-survivor1920×1381 258 KB
The actual Survivor interface at both sizes, using an isolated sample competition.
Sponsored Five gameweeks offer a fixed tCKB reward pool. Under the default terms, the top 5% qualify and share it in proportion to their points. The published gameweek rules govern eligibility; unsponsored weeks remain playable without a promised prize.
Anyone can bid to sponsor an eligible week, subject to its minimum. Top-ups combine, the winning eligible bid funds the pool, and losing bids are refunded. Sponsors can add a logo, website and introduction, or contribute without branding. These rewards use a disclosed custodial testnet wallet, separate from prediction contracts.
Come try one prediction
Streak is still in testnet beta. Testing covers database behavior, browser journeys, Rust scripts and signed local-chain transactions. Real wallet and matchday feedback matters too, especially whether payments, settlement and collection are clear from start to finish.
Open streakpitch.com, head to Markets, and explore an open fixture. Make a testnet prediction and follow it through Activity. Five offers a free alternative if you prefer to start with fantasy football.
Football is the starting point, not the limit. Other sports are planned as we add reliable data coverage and settlement rules suited to each one.
Which sport should come next? Basketball, cricket, tennis, MMA, esports, or something else? Drop your pick in the comments, along with the predictions you’d want to make.
I’d also welcome developers reviewing the CKB scripts and projects interested in sponsoring a gameweek.
Try Streak at streakpitch.com and tell me where the experience becomes unclear. Your feedback can help shape both the next improvements and the next sport.

recent_posts.topic_title: A Revenue Layer for CKB Nodes
recent_posts.author: psawyerberlin
recent_posts.content_text:
CKB Service Runner is ready to try: a free dashboard for your full node
Thanks to everyone in this thread: your feedback shaped what got built. The idea started as a “revenue layer”, and @janx, @joshyates1980, @LusoCryptoLabs, @Ayoub_Lesfer and @NightLantern turned it into something better: trust before money.
So the first release pays nobody. It’s a tool for node runners.
What you get today (mainnet and testnet)
A dashboard for your node: sync status, peers, node metrics, CPU/RAM/disk, all in one page.
A public node ranking by availability, sync, age and network diversity (ASN and region, never your IP). It’s summarised weekly in a cell on mainnet, so anyone can verify it.
It runs beside your node. No change to ckb, no consensus change, nothing runs unless you start it.
What it doesn’t do (yet)
No paid jobs on mainnet. The service runtime stays switched off until the network has run for 4 months with at least 20 diverse nodes. (I’ve lowered this from the 12 months / 60 nodes I mentioned earlier, so a pilot like CrowdCell’s keeper is realistic within a reasonable time.)
No payout per node. The ranking rewards reliability and age, not the number of nodes someone runs.
What’s shared
Your node ID, sync height, version and uptime, plus ASN and region for diversity. Never your IP address. You can switch the ranking off in the settings at any time.
Install
You need a fully synced CKB full node (or a Neuron full-node wallet) on the same machine.
GitHub - ckb-service-runner/ckb-service-runner: Side application for CKB full nodes: dashboard, node ranking, and a sandboxed service runtime · GitHub
Testnet testers welcome
On testnet the runtime is already live, with simulated jobs running around the clock. If you’d like to test the full flow (registration, jobs, tips), I’ll sponsor the testnet stake for the first testers. Just reply here.
What I’d love from you
Install it and tell me what breaks.
Tell me what you’d want the dashboard to show.
Every running node makes the ranking more meaningful, and gives future apps a real network to build on. Thanks for helping RUN CKB.

Ayoub_Lesfer:
CrowdCell’s
Thanks @Ayoub_Lesfer! Short answers to your two questions:
A job cell per campaign? Yes, with today’s CSR the run needs a job cell. It’s a separate cell the user creates, and it’s consumed in the settling transaction. Everything except the tip and the fee goes back to whoever funded it.
Paid by the transaction it settles? On chain that’s already possible, but CSR doesn’t build it yet. It would be a small runner change.
A possible option for CrowdCell users: a “settle automatically” checkbox when creating or backing. It adds a job cell with a 1–5 CKB tip, and a CSR runner finalizes the campaign or pays back the pledge after the deadline, so nobody has to come back to do it by hand. It would be optional and need no contract change, and the bot and fail-safe work as before. I’ve sent you a short concept privately; it’s entirely your call.

topics.title: CKB Devnet Explorer: a block explorer for your local OffCKB devnet

recent_posts.topic_title: CKB Devnet Explorer: a block explorer for your local OffCKB devnet
recent_posts.author: wildanrhmn
recent_posts.content_text:
Hi everyone,
For the past three months I’ve been in the CKBuilders program, and for my capstone I built a block explorer for the chain you test on every day: your local OffCKB devnet.
explorer-home1440×1180 207 KB
Why
Almost all of my time in the program was spent on a devnet started by offckb node. The official CKB Explorer can’t see that chain, and its backend (Rails, PostgreSQL, Redis and a block syncer) is far too heavy to run against a chain that offckb clean wipes all the time. So I read raw RPC JSON. My own scripts were 32-byte code hashes, cell data was hex, and when a transaction failed I dug through the node’s output.
In September I asked @RetricSu whether something like this already existed. He confirmed it was a real gap, and Neon agreed to let me build it as a standalone tool that could move into offckb later.
What it is
One Node process that reads your devnet node directly. There’s no database and no indexer service, and the only setup is one command. It follows the official explorer’s design system, so it should feel familiar, but it’s tuned for building rather than browsing:
It names your contracts: genesis scripts from offckb system-scripts, yours from deployment/scripts.json. A JS contract running on ckb-js-vm is named as the contract, not the VM.
It decodes every cell: contract code, sUDT/xUDT amounts, spores and clusters, DAO deposits and withdrawals, Type ID. A bar shows what each cell’s capacity pays for: lock, type, data, and what’s left unused.
It knows it’s on a devnet: it flags a deployment that offckb clean wiped, shows the node’s reason when a transaction is rejected, and rebuilds itself when the chain resets. There’s also a faucet and a page with offckb’s 20 test accounts.
Beyond that it has the pages you’d expect: blocks, transactions, the tx pool, addresses, scripts, tokens, NFTs, the Nervos DAO with estimated compensation, charts and tools.

Try it

Then open http://localhost:7070.
Into offckb
@RetricSu is adding sandboxed local plugins to offckb (offckb#542), with this explorer as the first one. He opened a PR on my repo for the plugin interface. I made the explorer run read-only inside his sandbox, and we’ll merge once his side is ready.
What it doesn’t do (yet)
It’s for devnets only, on purpose. Mainnet pages like halving, Fiber, RGB++ and price data are left out.
It runs on your own machine. There’s no hosted demo yet; I’m working on one so you can try it without installing anything.
The final step of a DAO withdrawal isn’t covered yet, because the lock period on a devnet is about 18.8 days and I haven’t waited it out.
Data stored by JS contracts (for example a counter’s u64) still shows as hex.
I’d love to hear
If you build on a devnet: what do you still check by hand that an explorer should show you?
Should this stay a standalone tool, live inside offckb, or both?
Of what’s missing above, what would you want first?

recent_posts.topic_title: CKBdapps 2.0：为 CKB 生态重新搭建的项目目录
recent_posts.author: yixiu.ckbfans.bit
recent_posts.content_text:
大家好，也许有一部分小伙伴已经注意到了，CKBdapps（https://ckbdapps.com ）刚刚完成了一次彻底的改版。接下来这篇帖子我想和大家分享这次我们改了什么、为什么这样改，以及大家可以怎样参与。
为什么要重写
CKBdapps 从 2023 年初开始构建，并于同年 6 月正式上线，它的定位是 CKB 生态的项目目录，为用户在 CKB 这块土地上导航。然而，随着生态的发展，我们发现最难的不是写页面、写功能，而是让 CKBdapps 上的项目信息一直保持正确。旧版网站在这件事上越来越吃力：
数据分散。 一个项目的信息分散在好几个 JSON 文件里，列表、配置和详情各管一部分。加一个项目要改好几处，改漏了也看不出来。
手写的内容太多。 亮点、FAQ、透明度清单都靠人工撰写，写的时候是对的，过几个月就过时了，也没人知道哪里过时。

1. 一个项目一个文件，最少 5 行。
每个项目就是仓库里的一个 Markdown 文件：名称、网址、一句话介绍、分类、核对日期，写满 5 行就能提交。简介、GitHub 仓库、链上合约、审计报告都是可选的。字段越少，过时的地方就越少。
2. 能推导的信息不再手写。
分组、标签、相似项目、活跃度、网站状态、信息是否过时，全部由程序根据数据计算出来，不需要任何人维护。旧版的亮点、FAQ、透明度清单，我们都去掉了。
3. 活跃度交给 CKB Pulse。
项目的活跃度数据来自 CKB Pulse，每小时更新一次，不需要项目方手动提交任何东西。我们自己不用搭建和维护数据采集服务，CKBdapps 也因此不用保存任何 GitHub 或 X 的密钥。
4. 过时的信息会被标出来，而不是被藏起来。
每个项目都有一个“核对于”日期。超过一年没有核对的页面会显示一条提示，邀请项目方提交更新，但页面本身不会被隐藏。
5. 机器做检查，人做判断。
每个 PR 都会自动校验文件格式和分类，写错了会直接报错。
每周自动检查所有外部链接，找出打不开的网站。
每周自动从 CKB Pulse 和 Nervos Talk 的双周报里寻找还没有被收录的项目，生成一个草稿 PR。这一步只负责“发现”，每个候选项目都要经过人工审核才会合并：它必须已经在 CKB 或 Fiber 主网上线，并且现在就能使用。
测试网原型的演示网站每小时检查一次，打不开时页面会如实告诉大家。
接下来，我们也在考虑引入 AI 来分担一部分审核和整理工作，让新项目从被发现到被收录的过程更快。

每个项目页的右侧都展示了这个项目的源文件，旁边是一个“在 GitHub 编辑”的按钮。项目方发现信息不对，点一下就可以直接提交修改。

怎样参与
说了这么多，CKBdapps 终究是大家的目录。它能不能一直准确、一直有新意，靠的是每一位建设者和用户的参与。下面是几种参与的方式：
提交或更新项目： 打开 提交项目 · CKBdapps ，按页面说明新建一个文件，提交一个 PR。仓库的提交历史里，每个项目都是单独的一次提交，可以照着参考。
提交测试网原型： 和提交普通项目一样，只需要多写一行 testnet: true。收录标准是：能在 CKB 测试网上运行；代码开源并带有许可证；做了目录里还没有的事；作者本人同意被收录。
反馈问题： 欢迎在这个帖子下回复，或者在 GitHub 上提 issue。每一条反馈我们都会认真看。
致谢
这次改版，并非我们几个人关起门来实施的。很多关键的决定，都来自社区朋友们的一句提醒、一次追问。
Hanssen：在“怎样可持续地维护”、“项目展示的规则如何做到公平”“、还在建设中的项目要怎样才能被列出来”这些问题上， @Hanssen 给了我们很多启发。这些问题归根结底指向同一件事：怎样让开发者在 CKBdapps 上获得成功。这句话，后来成了我们这次改版的方向。
Jacky：作为新版本 ckbdapps 的首位体验官， @JackyLHH 在页面的UI/UX方面提供了多个建设性建议均已被落地实施。
Neon： @neon.bit 建议我们将 CKBuilder 计划里的项目收录进来，这与 @Hanssen 提到的还在建设中的项目要怎样才能被列出来”不谋而合。让我们认真思考那些“还没上主网”的作品该放在哪里，也直接促成了“测试网原型”这个页面。
CKB Pulse（LusoCryptoLabs）：感谢 @LusoCryptoLabs 为项目页提供活跃度数据，并且和我们约定好了接口的稳定性。有了你们，CKBdapps 不用再自己维护一套数据采集服务，就能让大家一眼看到每个项目前进的步伐。
最后，还要感谢每一位在 CKB 上建设的朋友。不管你的项目是已经服务着真实的用户，还是只是测试网上一个刚刚跑通的小想法，你们都是这片土地上最珍贵的部分。CKBdapps 想做的，只是把你们的作品，好好地摆在大家面前。
欢迎来逛逛，也欢迎把你的项目插进来：https://ckbdapps.com

有一些项目，可能永远不会上主网——上主网意味着要为用户的资产负责，要有持续运营的能力，这对一个人、一个周末的灵感来说，确实是很重的担子。但它们在测试网上把一个想法实实在在地跑通了：用 CKB 的 cell 做一个链上众筹，在一个 cell 里装下一整盘棋，把线下活动的签到做成不可转让的徽章……

这些作品，过去没有地方可以放。它们不够“正式”，进不了项目目录；可它们又那么有意思，证明了 CKB 能做到的事情。我们不想让这些心血就这样沉在某个 GitHub 仓库里。

所以我们为它们开了一个单独的页面。每一个原型都是开源的，你可以看代码、领一点测试币亲手试一试，也许下一个把它带上主网的人，就是你。而那些愿意把自己的创意贡献出来的建设者，值得被看见，也应该被记住。

image2382×698 53.4 KB

  • 生态图。 首页的最后，是一张生态全景图。每个收录的项目占一格，按钱包、应用、资产与身份、基础设施、生态伙伴五个分组排列，紫色描边的格子是独立建设者的项目。它不是又一份项目列表，而是一张地图：一眼看清生态的全貌，点一下某个分组，就会跳到“探索”页里对应的筛选结果。

image1920×1800 320 KB

探索：完整的项目目录

在这里可以按分组、分类筛选，也可以只看独立建设者的项目，列表和网格两种视图随意切换。筛选条件都写在网址里，复制链接发给朋友，对方打开看到的就是同样的结果。

image2368×1726 299 KB

项目页：每个项目都有自己的家

每个项目都有一个独立的网址，适合分享，也能被搜索引擎收录。页面上除了项目的简介，还有：

  • 活跃度：这部分数据来自 CKB Pulse，它持续追踪 CKB 生态在 GitHub 上的公开动态。只要项目写了 GitHub 仓库，页面就会显示最近 30 天每天的动态和最近的几条更新，并标注“活跃”“放缓”或“沉寂”。“沉寂”只表示最近没有公开动态，并不代表项目已经停止。
  • 链上合约：项目在 CKB 上使用的合约及其 code hash。
  • 审计报告：如果有的话，会列在这里。
  • 相似项目：根据分类自动推荐。

没有数据的部分不会显示。所以哪怕一个项目只写了 5 行信息，它的页面也是完整、体面的。

image1920×3512 457 KB

减半：一起等待下一次减半

页面直接从 CKB 主网节点读取最新区块，实时倒计时下一次减半，并展示完整的减半时间表和原理说明。

image1920×2718 271 KB

数据：把几张图放在同一段时间里看

这里有 CKB 的供应量分布、Nervos DAO 锁仓，以及历史价格、全网算力和链上占用的走势图。

和旧版相比，最大的变化是：所有图表共用一个时间范围。旧版每张图都有自己独立的缩放，想对比同一时期的价格和算力，得把几张图分别拖到同一段时间，很难对齐。新版只需选一次 7 天、1 个月、6 个月、1 年或全部，或者拖动下面的时间轴，所有图表就会一起切换到同一段时间。这样就能很直观地看到，同一个周期里，价格、算力和链上占用各自发生了什么。

鼠标或方向键移到某一天，就能读到那一天的数值；每张图也都可以“以表格查看”。

image1920×4272 460 KB

提交项目：一页说清楚

怎样提交项目，一页就能说清楚：一个模板文件、一个预填好的 GitHub 新建文件链接，以及每个字段的说明。

image1936×2448 444 KB

给 AI 和开发者

以上这些页面都是给人看的。新版里，除了提供给大家浏览的网页之外，我们还提供了两个给机器读的文件，让 CKBdapps 的数据也能流进别人的工具里：

  • ckbdapps.com/llms.txt ： 一份按 llms.txt 惯例写成的网站索引，列出了所有项目、它们的分类和一句话介绍。当你问 AI 助手“CKB 上有哪些钱包”时，它可以从这里读到一份准确、最新的答案，而不是凭印象猜。
  • ckbdapps.com/projects.json： 所有项目的完整数据，包括分类、链接、GitHub 仓库、合约、收录日期等。如果你在做钱包、浏览器、数据看板或者任何需要 CKB 项目列表的工具，可以直接拿去用，不用再自己整理一份。

这两个文件和网站一起更新，数据始终保持一致。

规则透明：不靠人工挑选

前面介绍了新版的样子和各个页面的功能。接下来，想和大家分享一个我们在改版时反复讨论、也最看重的问题：项目是怎么被摆到大家面前的。

做项目目录，最容易被问到的问题就是：“凭什么它排在前面？”

我们的回答是：首页上没有任何一个位置是人工挑选的。 每个版块都由一条写在公开代码里的规则决定：

版块 规则
猜你喜欢 第一次访问时，从应用、钱包、资产与身份三个分组中随机抽取，每个项目机会均等。看过几个项目后，按你看过的项目的分类推荐。浏览记录只保存在你自己的浏览器里。
最新收录 按收录日期，显示最新的 3 个。
独立建设者 从所有独立建设者的项目中随机抽取 5 个，每个项目机会均等。
测试网原型 从所有测试网原型中随机抽取 3 个，每个项目机会均等，网站每次更新时重新抽取。
探索 先按分组，再按名称字母顺序排列。

同一个项目不会同时出现在首页的两个版块里。“猜你喜欢”和“独立建设者”的随机抽取在每位访客自己的浏览器里进行，每次打开都不一样。

我们怎样解决维护难的问题

规则定好了，还得有人一直把它执行下去，项目信息也得一直保持正确。还记得开头提到的那几个痛点吗？数据分散、手写内容容易过时、看不出项目是否还活着、新项目没人发现。这一部分，就来说说我们是怎样一个一个解决它们的。

1. 一个项目一个文件，最少 5 行。
每个项目就是仓库里的一个 Markdown 文件：名称、网址、一句话介绍、分类、核对日期，写满 5 行就能提交。简介、GitHub 仓库、链上合约、审计报告都是可选的。字段越少，过时的地方就越少。

2. 能推导的信息不再手写。
分组、标签、相似项目、活跃度、网站状态、信息是否过时，全部由程序根据数据计算出来，不需要任何人维护。旧版的亮点、FAQ、透明度清单，我们都去掉了。

3. 活跃度交给 CKB Pulse。
项目的活跃度数据来自 CKB Pulse，每小时更新一次，不需要项目方手动提交任何东西。我们自己不用搭建和维护数据采集服务，CKBdapps 也因此不用保存任何 GitHub 或 X 的密钥。

4. 过时的信息会被标出来，而不是被藏起来。
每个项目都有一个“核对于”日期。超过一年没有核对的页面会显示一条提示，邀请项目方提交更新，但页面本身不会被隐藏。

5. 机器做检查，人做判断。

  • 每个 PR 都会自动校验文件格式和分类，写错了会直接报错。
  • 每周自动检查所有外部链接，找出打不开的网站。
  • 每周自动从 CKB Pulse 和 Nervos Talk 的双周报里寻找还没有被收录的项目，生成一个草稿 PR。这一步只负责“发现”，每个候选项目都要经过人工审核才会合并：它必须已经在 CKB 或 Fiber 主网上线，并且现在就能使用。
  • 测试网原型的演示网站每小时检查一次，打不开时页面会如实告诉大家。

接下来，我们也在考虑引入 AI 来分担一部分审核和整理工作，让新项目从被发现到被收录的过程更快。

6. 人人都可以修改。
每个项目页的右侧都展示了这个项目的源文件，旁边是一个“在 GitHub 编辑”的按钮。项目方发现信息不对，点一下就可以直接提交修改。

另外，为了控制维护成本，我们也做了一些减法：旧版的活动页面和收藏功能已经下线，旧的网址会自动跳转到新页面。

怎样参与

说了这么多，CKBdapps 终究是大家的目录。它能不能一直准确、一直有新意，靠的是每一位建设者和用户的参与。下面是几种参与的方式：

  • 提交或更新项目： 打开 提交项目 · CKBdapps ，按页面说明新建一个文件，提交一个 PR。仓库的提交历史里，每个项目都是单独的一次提交，可以照着参考。
  • 提交测试网原型： 和提交普通项目一样，只需要多写一行 testnet: true。收录标准是：能在 CKB 测试网上运行；代码开源并带有许可证；做了目录里还没有的事；作者本人同意被收录。
  • 反馈问题： 欢迎在这个帖子下回复，或者在 GitHub 上提 issue。每一条反馈我们都会认真看。

致谢

这次改版，并非我们几个人关起门来实施的。很多关键的决定，都来自社区朋友们的一句提醒、一次追问。

  • Hanssen：在“怎样可持续地维护”、“项目展示的规则如何做到公平”“、还在建设中的项目要怎样才能被列出来”这些问题上， @Hanssen 给了我们很多启发。这些问题归根结底指向同一件事：怎样让开发者在 CKBdapps 上获得成功。这句话，后来成了我们这次改版的方向。
  • Jacky：作为新版本 ckbdapps 的首位体验官， @JackyLHH 在页面的UI/UX方面提供了多个建设性建议均已被落地实施。
  • Neon： @neon.bit 建议我们将 CKBuilder 计划里的项目收录进来，这与 @Hanssen 提到的还在建设中的项目要怎样才能被列出来”不谋而合。让我们认真思考那些“还没上主网”的作品该放在哪里，也直接促成了“测试网原型”这个页面。
  • CKB Pulse（LusoCryptoLabs）：感谢 @LusoCryptoLabs 为项目页提供活跃度数据，并且和我们约定好了接口的稳定性。有了你们，CKBdapps 不用再自己维护一套数据采集服务，就能让大家一眼看到每个项目前进的步伐。

最后，还要感谢每一位在 CKB 上建设的朋友。不管你的项目是已经服务着真实的用户，还是只是测试网上一个刚刚跑通的小想法，你们都是这片土地上最珍贵的部分。CKBdapps 想做的，只是把你们的作品，好好地摆在大家面前。

欢迎来逛逛，也欢迎把你的项目插进来：https://ckbdapps.com

recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | TapFiber: Fiber Payment Intent and Verifiable Receipt Reference
recent_posts.author: vida
recent_posts.content_text:
1. Project Overview
Project name: TapFiber
One-sentence summary: An open-source Fiber payment-intent kit that binds a merchant order to one exact invoice, accepts settlement once and produces a signed receipt; NFC and QR are the first physical delivery methods for the request.
Project type: Core library + testnet FNN integration + reference terminal + reproducible failure report.
Funding requested: US$900 paid in CKB
Duration: 5 weeks
TapFiber is not another checkout page and it is not an NFC hardware project. Its core is the boundary between a Fiber invoice and a fulfilled real-world order:
Payment request → exact Fiber settlement → one terminal state → verifiable receipt
NFC is the first reference transport because it makes the boundary easy to test in person. The same signed request can be carried by a QR code, a browser link, or a future wallet deep-link.
2. Team Profile
I am a blockchain product engineer who has built across Solana, EVM and Bitcoin with additional work in Move and Stellar
Recent work:
Knapstore: a Solana protocol with a signed publishing and commitment flow. The work included Ed25519 instruction verification, PDA-bound publisher authorization, on-chain key rotation and recovery paths, tombstoned key history and adversarial authorization tests
Paymod: a programmable payment-authority system for agent-initiated transfers, with deterministic policy checks, human approval through Telegram and an auditable approval trail
I am new to building directly on Fiber. That is why TapFiber is scoped as an open, testnet-only reference implementation with pinned FNN compatibility evidence, reproducible tests and explicit failure reporting not as a claim of production merchant readiness
The relevant experience for TapFiber is not simply having used multiple chains. It is having built systems where a cryptographic action must be bound to the correct request, state transition, authorization rule, and audit record. TapFiber applies that discipline to a narrow Fiber question: when can an application safely treat a payment as fulfilling one exact order?
